items.title: AI Panic at Apple: New CEO John Ternus Tells Software Chief Siri Fixes Are Not Enough
items.summary:
Turning a voice assistant into an autonomous agent is harder than shipping a new chip.

Making Siri genuinely capable runs into real obstacles: privacy constraints, permissions architecture, and reliable execution at scale. Apple built its advantage around deep hardware-software integration, while competitors have pursued rapid AI-model iteration. Reconciling those two philosophies takes time, and time is a resource under pressure.

## An Organization Built for a Different Clock [...] ## Margin Pressure Arrives at the Wrong Moment

Rising memory costs and slowing services growth are tightening the window for a successful AI pivot.

Rising memory-chip prices are expected to squeeze Apple's margins and could push product prices higher, according to Reuters. Analysts cited by Reuters also expect services-business growth to slow compared with earlier periods, raising the stakes for AI-powered offerings to generate new momentum.

## Regulators Add Another Constraint [...] AAPL

  +2.28%

Apple is reporting strong iPhone sales while its new CEO privately presses his software chief to move faster on artificial intelligence. Those two facts sitting side by side reveal the bind Ternus stepped into on September 1, 2026. The company's investment in AI chips signals how seriously Apple takes the competitive pressure.

## The New CEO's First Real Test

Ternus came up through hardware. His most urgent problem is software.
